text:
AI-native app runtime architecture

An AI-native app runtime architecture is the production environment for applications in which AI models or agents are core runtime components rather than optional integrations. Unlike a conventional deterministic runtime, it must coordinate probabilistic model output, contextual data, tools, policies, and feedback.

Core runtime components

- Experience and API layer receives user, system, and event-driven requests.
- AI gateway routes requests across models and manages authentication, quotas, caching, cost, and failover.
- Agent or workflow orchestrator plans tasks, manages multi-step execution, and coordinates specialized agents.
- Context layer assembles prompts using session state, memory, enterprise data, vector retrieval, and knowledge graphs.
- Model layer provides language, vision, speech, embedding, and domain-specific inference.
- Tool and integration layer lets agents call approved APIs, databases, business systems, and automation services.
- State and data layer stores conversations, workflow state, application data, embeddings, and audit records.
- Trust layer enforces identity, authorization, privacy, content safety, grounding, validation, and human approvals.
- Observability and evaluation layer records traces, prompts, responses, tool calls, quality, latency, cost, and safety outcomes.
- Feedback loop uses production evidence to improve prompts, retrieval, policies, workflows, and models through controlled releases.

Typical execution flow

A request is authenticated, enriched with relevant context, routed to an appropriate model or agent, and processed through one or more model and tool calls. Policies validate each sensitive action, the runtime persists state and evidence, and telemetry feeds continuous evaluation and improvement.

Platform-neutral description: There is no single standard AI-native runtime architecture. Exact components depend on whether the application uses simple model calls, retrieval-augmented generation, autonomous agents, real-time data, or regulated workflows.
limitations: No specific platform or product was identified, so this describes the generic architectural concept rather than confirmed product capabilities.
